en: to take part in; to side with (usually something bad or illegal)

examples.ko: 그 사람은 범죄에 가담한 적이 없어요.
examples.en: That person has never been involved in any crime.
My friends joined the fight, and things got worse.
Is there anyone who will join this plan?
There is a rumor going around that someone took part in the fraud case.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일에 가담하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to get involved in that.
Nobody joined, so the plan fell through.

explain: '참가하다'는 대회나 모임처럼 평범한 자리에 쓰지만, '가담하다'는 주로 나쁜 일이나 한쪽 편에 힘을 보탤 때 써요. 좋은 행사에 '가담하다'를 쓰면 어색해요.
explain_en: 참가하다 is for ordinary events and contests, but 가담하다 is mostly used when someone joins in something bad or takes one side. Using it for a nice event sounds odd.

dis.h: get involved, usually in something bad

p.n: 범죄에 참여했어요 sounds odd. 가담하다 carries a negative nuance, while 참여하다 is neutral.

examples.ko: 농부가 봄이 오기 전에 밭을 갈아엎었어요.
examples.en: The farmer plowed the field before spring came.

examples.ko: 이 땅을 갈아엎고 옥수수를 심을 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to plow this land and plant corn.
I can hear the sound of a tractor plowing the rice field.

examples.ko: 계획이 마음에 안 들어서 처음부터 갈아엎기로 했어요.
examples.en: I didn't like the plan, so I decided to scrap it and start over.
The freshly plowed field smelled of earth.
My team leader told us to overhaul the proposal completely.

explain: 기본 뜻은 쟁기나 트랙터로 땅을 뒤집는 거예요. 그래서 계획이나 방식을 처음부터 완전히 새로 하자고 할 때 '싹 갈아엎다'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: Its basic meaning is turning over soil with a plow or tractor. Because of that, people also use it figuratively, as in '싹 갈아엎다', to mean completely redoing a plan or method from scratch.

examples.en: The subway on my commute these days is real torture.

examples.ko: 여름에 에어컨 없이 지내는 건 고역이었어요.
examples.en: Getting through summer without air conditioning was an ordeal.

examples.ko: 매일 두 시간씩 걷는 일이 저에게는 고역이에요.
examples.en: Walking two hours every day is a real chore for me.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들고 계단을 오르는 고역을 겪었어요.
examples.en: I went through the ordeal of climbing stairs with heavy bags.

examples.ko: 이 일이 고역처럼 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times when this work feels like drudgery.

examples.ko: 긴 회의를 가만히 듣고 있는 것도 고역이에요.
examples.en: Sitting through a long meeting is also a torment.

explain: '힘들다'보다 하기 싫고 괴로운 일이라는 느낌이 강해요. '고역이다', '고역을 치르다', '고역을 겪다'처럼 쓰고, 사람이 아니라 '일'이나 '상황'이 주어가 돼요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '힘들다', suggesting something unpleasant and painful to go through. It appears in '고역이다', '고역을 치르다', and '고역을 겪다', and the subject is a task or situation, not a person.

examples.en: The pilgrims prayed as they walked the path of penance.
This hike was practically an ordeal.

examples.ko: 매일 새벽에 일어나는 게 저에게는 고행이에요.
examples.en: Getting up at dawn every day is torture for me.
I heard the monk practiced asceticism in the mountains.
The subway on my commute feels like an ordeal.
A marathon is closer to an ordeal than to fun.

explain: 원래는 종교에서 몸을 괴롭히며 하는 수행을 뜻하지만, 일상에서는 정말 힘든 일을 조금 과장해서 '고행 같다'고 말해요. '고생'보다 스스로 견뎌 내야 하는 힘든 일이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Originally it means religious training that puts the body through pain, but in daily life people exaggerate and say something is '고행 같다' when it is really tough. Compared with '고생', it feels more like an ordeal you have to endure yourself.

en: to come to a standstill; to become bogged down; to be deadlocked

examples.ko: 협상이 몇 달째 교착해서 아무 결론이 안 나요.
examples.en: The negotiations have been deadlocked for months, so there's no conclusion.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 대화가 교착하면 경제에도 영향이 있어요.
examples.en: If talks between the two countries stall, the economy is affected too.

examples.ko: 교착한 상황을 풀려고 새 제안을 내놓았어요.
examples.en: They made a new proposal to break the deadlock.

examples.ko: 회의가 교착해도 포기하지 말고 계속 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: Even if the meeting gets stuck, let's not give up and keep talking.
I saw on the news that the labor-management talks hit a deadlock.
The matter that had been stuck finally got resolved.

explain: 보통은 '교착 상태에 빠지다'라고 많이 말해요. 협상, 대화, 경제 같은 큰 일에 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '막혀 있어요', '꼼짝도 못 해요'라고 해요.
explain_en: People usually say '교착 상태에 빠지다' (fall into a deadlock). It is used for big matters like negotiations, talks or the economy, while in everyday talk people say '막혀 있어요' or '꼼짝도 못 해요'.

examples.en: The hero saved the villagers.

examples.ko: 위험에 빠진 아이들을 구원한 소방관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a firefighter who rescued children in danger.
I felt that music saved me.
Who will save this country?

examples.ko: 위기에 빠진 회사를 구원하고 싶어서 직접 나섰어요.
examples.en: I stepped in myself because I wanted to save the company from the crisis.

examples.ko: 종교가 사람을 구원한다고 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe religion saves people.

explain: 일상에서는 '구하다', '도와주다'를 쓰고, 구원하다는 큰 위기나 종교에서 사람을 건진다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 영화나 소설에서 '세상을 구원하다'처럼 나와요. 작은 도움에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: In daily life Koreans say '구하다' or '도와주다'; 구원하다 carries a heavy sense of rescuing someone from a great crisis or in a religious sense. It appears in films and novels, as in '세상을 구원하다'. It does not suit small favors.

dis.h: save from suffering or sin, deliverance

p.n: 구조하다 would sound like a physical rescue, not spiritual salvation.

examples.en: I was suddenly asked a question and got cornered.
Thanks to my friend, I got out of a tight spot.

examples.ko: 상대 팀을 궁지로 몰아넣는 작전이 통했어요.
examples.en: The tactic of driving the opposing team into a corner worked.

examples.ko: 궁지에 몰린 상대는 오히려 더 세게 덤벼요.
examples.en: A cornered opponent comes at you even harder.
He escaped the predicament with a single remark.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 회사가 큰 궁지에 처했어요.
examples.en: Because of this matter, the company is in a serious predicament.

explain: 보통 '궁지에 몰리다/빠지다/처하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. '곤경'과 비슷하지만, 궁지는 도망갈 곳 없이 몰린 느낌이 더 강해요. 벗어날 때는 '궁지에서 벗어나다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 궁지에 몰린 쥐가 고양이를 문다더니, 약한 팀이 끝까지 달려들었어요.
phrases.en: They say a cornered rat bites the cat, and the weaker team kept fighting to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절박한 상황에 몰리면 약한 사람도 강한 상대에게 필사적으로 덤빈다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb saying that even the weak will fight desperately against a stronger opponent when driven into a corner.
phrases.en_equiv: a cornered rat will fight back

explain_en: It usually goes with '에', as in '궁지에 몰리다/빠지다/처하다'. It is similar to '곤경' (hardship), but '궁지' conveys more strongly the feeling of being backed into a corner with no way out. To get out you say '궁지에서 벗어나다'.

examples.en: I meant to rest for a moment but just ended up staying put.

examples.ko: 친구 집에서 며칠 묵으려다 한 달이나 눌러앉았어요.
examples.en: I meant to stay at my friend's place a few days but ended up staying a whole month.
That player decided to stay with the team.
Is it okay if I just stay here?

examples.ko: 서울에 잠시 온 건데 십 년째 눌러앉아 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I only came to Seoul for a while, but I've ended up living here for ten years.
What do we do if the guest doesn't leave and just stays?

explain: 가려던 곳으로 안 가고 그 자리에 계속 머물게 될 때 써요. '머무르다'가 중립적인 말이라면, 이 말은 '어쩌다 오래 있게 됐다'는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when you don't go where you meant to and keep staying put. While '머무르다' is neutral, this word carries a feeling of ending up staying longer than planned.

examples.en: As the seclusion dragged on, fans grew worried.

examples.ko: 작가는 두문불출 끝에 새 소설을 완성했어요.
examples.en: After a long seclusion, the author finished a new novel.

examples.ko: 두문불출 중인 친구에게 안부 메시지를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent a check-in message to my friend who is staying shut in.
He stayed shut in all vacation, so Mom is worried.
As his reclusion went on, rumors spread.

examples.ko: 두문불출 생활을 끝내고 오랜만에 밖으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: I ended my life of staying shut in and went outside for the first time in a long while.

explain: 집에 틀어박혀 밖에 나가지 않는 것을 뜻하는 네 글자 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 유명인이나 작가가 모습을 보이지 않을 때 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '집에 틀어박혀 있다'고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This four-character expression means shutting yourself in and not going out. It often appears in news and writing when a celebrity or author is out of sight, while in everyday talk people say '집에 틀어박혀 있다'.

examples.en: As soon as we opened the door, customers rushed in all at once.
When a typhoon comes, waves surge onto the shore.
People flooded in at lunchtime, and it was hectic.

examples.ko: 연말에는 일이 한꺼번에 밀어닥치는 때가 많아요.
examples.en: At the end of the year, work often piles up all at once.
I'm worried that reporters will suddenly swarm in.

examples.ko: 세일 첫날 사람들이 밀어닥치면서 가게가 난리였어요.
examples.en: On the first day of the sale, people poured in and the store was chaos.

explain: 사람, 물, 일이 큰 힘으로 한꺼번에 몰려올 때 써요. '몰려오다'보다 기세가 센 느낌이에요. '일이 밀어닥치다'처럼 일이나 변화가 갑자기 많아질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when people, water or work come all at once with great force. It feels stronger than '몰려오다'. It is also used for a sudden flood of work or change, as in '일이 밀어닥치다'.

examples.en: The baby is crying and kicking his legs about.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 아끼며 살아도 돈이 잘 안 모여요.
examples.en: Even though I struggle to save, money doesn't build up.
The fly caught in the spider web is struggling and squirming.
He worked desperately to pay off his debt.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 애를 써도 일이 풀리지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I strain, things don't work out.
The child is wriggling around to be picked up.

explain: 팔다리를 작게 흔들며 애쓰는 모습을 말해요. 아기나 작은 동물 이야기뿐 아니라 '바둥바둥 살다'처럼 힘들게 노력하는 모습에도 써요. 약간 안쓰러운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It shows small arms and legs moving as one tries hard. It is used for babies and small animals, and also for people working hard against difficulty, as in '바둥바둥 살다'. It carries a slightly pitiful feeling.

examples.en: The child snapped a branch just for fun.
You must not snap the chopsticks.
I got angry and snapped the pencil.
We snapped off branches and made a fire.
We broke the cookie in half and shared it.
Please don't snap that stick.

explain: '부러뜨리다'와 비슷한데 손으로 힘을 줘서 뚝 꺾는 느낌이 더 강해요. 가늘고 긴 것에 주로 써요. '르' 불규칙이라서 '분질러요', '분질렀어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is close to '부러뜨리다' but feels more like snapping something off sharply with your hands, usually something thin and long. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '분질러요' and '분질렀어요'.

examples.en: I got sick from exhaustion of my energy.
The project stopped because the budget ran out.
Burnout is called exhaustion of the mind.
The discount lasts only until stock runs out.
I was so worn out that I took a day off.

examples.ko: 자원 소진을 막기 위해 아껴 써야 해요.
examples.en: We have to use things sparingly to prevent depletion of resources.

explain: 소진은 가진 힘, 돈, 물건이 다 써서 바닥나는 것을 말해요. 안내문에서는 '재고 소진 시까지', '예산 소진'처럼 쓰고, 사람의 상태를 말할 때는 '번아웃'과 비슷한 '탈진' 느낌이에요. 말로 할 때는 '다 떨어지다', '바닥나다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Sojin means running out of strength, money, or goods until nothing is left. Notices use it in phrases like 재고 소진 시까지 and 예산 소진, and for people it is close to burnout or 탈진. In speech, 다 떨어지다 and 바닥나다 are far more natural.

en: be settled; be brought under control; be sorted out

examples.en: I'm glad the accident was dealt with quickly.
It takes time until the confusion is sorted out.
Only after the fight was settled did everyone smile.
The problem wasn't resolved, so the meeting dragged on.
I'll contact you as soon as things are under control.
It was a big mistake, but it was handled well.

explain: 수습되다는 어지럽거나 문제가 된 일이 정리되어 가라앉을 때 써요. 사고, 소동, 논란처럼 일이 터진 뒤의 말과 잘 어울려요. 소리가 같은 '수습 사원'의 수습은 다른 말이니 따로 외우세요.
explain_en: 수습되다 is used when a messy or troublesome situation gets sorted out and calms down. It pairs with accidents, commotions and controversies, that is, things after trouble has broken out. The 수습 in 수습 사원 (trainee) sounds the same but is a different word.

en: to confess; to tell the whole truth

examples.ko: 사실 그 보고서를 끝까지 읽지 못했다고 팀장님께 실토했어요.
examples.en: I confessed to my team leader that I had not actually finished reading the report.

examples.ko: 잘못을 실토하는 사람에게는 화를 내기보다 해결책을 함께 찾아 주세요.
examples.en: For someone who admits a mistake, please help find a solution instead of getting angry.
My friend finally came clean about the secret.

examples.ko: 솔직하게 실토하면 마음이 좀 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: If you confess honestly, you will probably feel a bit more at ease.

examples.ko: 동생은 엄마가 물어보자 바로 실토해 버렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling came clean right away when Mom asked.
No one knew until he confessed.

explain: 숨기고 싶던 잘못이나 비밀을 어쩔 수 없이 털어놓을 때 써요. '고백하다'는 마음이나 감정에도 쓰지만 '실토하다'는 숨겼던 사실에 어울려요. '털어놓다'보다 조금 더 잘못을 시인하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you are forced to reveal a mistake or secret you wanted to hide. '고백하다' can also be used for feelings, but '실토하다' fits facts that were being concealed. It feels a bit more like admitting wrongdoing than '털어놓다'.

examples.en: I lost in a ridiculous way, but I actually ended up laughing.

examples.ko: 어처구니없이 간단한 실수 때문에 일을 망쳤어요.
examples.en: I ruined the job because of an absurdly simple mistake.

examples.ko: 그는 어처구니없이 긴 줄을 보고 포기했어요.
examples.en: He saw the ridiculously long line and gave up.
I was shocked that it sold for an absurdly high price.
Can you believe I stupidly lost the documents?
The fight that started over something ridiculous lasted a long time.

explain: 기가 막히고 황당한 일을 말할 때 써요. '어이없이', '황당하게'와 비슷하고, 보통 좋지 않거나 믿기 어려운 일에 붙어요. 형용사 '어처구니없다'의 활용형이라 '어처구니없는 일'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things that are so absurd they leave you stunned. It is close to '어이없이' and '황당하게', and usually attaches to bad or hard-to-believe events. It is the adverb form of the adjective '어처구니없다', which also appears as in '어처구니없는 일'.

examples.ko: 그는 하루 한 끼로 겨우 연명했어요.
examples.en: He barely survived on one meal a day.

examples.ko: 일자리를 잃은 뒤 아르바이트로 연명하고 있어요.
examples.en: After losing my job, I'm getting by on part-time work.

examples.ko: 전쟁 중에 사람들은 풀뿌리로 연명했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say people survived on roots during the war.

examples.ko: 빚으로 연명하는 생활을 이제 끝내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to end this life of getting by on debt.
It's tight even to scrape by on a small pension.

examples.ko: 가게는 대출로 연명하다가 결국 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The shop kept going on loans and finally closed.

explain: '겨우', '간신히'와 같이 쓰이며 어렵게 목숨이나 생활을 이어 간다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~로 연명하다'처럼 수단을 앞에 둬요. 병원 뉴스에서 '연명 치료'라는 말도 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used with '겨우' or '간신히' and gives the feeling of barely keeping life or livelihood going. The means usually comes first, as in '~로 연명하다'. You may also hear '연명 치료' in hospital-related news.

examples.en: The police held back the crowd that was rushing in.
The guard stopped us, so we could not go inside.
I turned back after being stopped by the guard.
My friend tried to stop me, but it was no use.

examples.ko: 아무 제지 없이 건물에 들어갈 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I was able to enter the building without anyone stopping me.
Despite the teacher's attempt to stop them, the children kept chattering.

explain: '말리다'는 일상에서 누군가의 행동을 말릴 때 쓰고, '제지하다'는 경찰·경비원처럼 막을 힘이 있는 사람이 막을 때 자주 써요. '제지를 받다', '제지를 당하다'처럼 쓰고, 막는 쪽은 '제지하다'예요.
explain_en: 말리다 is the everyday word for talking someone out of an action, while 제지하다 is often used when someone with authority, like police or a guard, stops people. You say '제지를 받다' or '제지를 당하다' for being stopped, and 제지하다 for the one stopping.

examples.ko: 경찰이 중무장 상태로 건물 앞을 지키고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are guarding the front of the building heavily armed.

examples.ko: 중무장을 한 군인들이 도로를 막고 있어요.
examples.en: Heavily armed soldiers are blocking the road.

examples.ko: 겨울 산에 갈 때는 중무장이 필수예요.
examples.en: When you go up a mountain in winter, bundling up heavily is a must.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 국경에 중무장 부대를 배치했어요.
examples.en: This country has stationed a heavily armed unit at the border.

examples.ko: 중무장한 병사들이 마을 입구에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: Heavily armed soldiers were standing at the entrance of the village.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 온 날에는 중무장 차림으로 출근하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: On days with a lot of snow, many people go to work bundled up like they're going to battle.

explain: 군대나 경찰 이야기에서 주로 나오지만, 추운 날 옷을 잔뜩 껴입은 모습을 농담처럼 '중무장'이라고도 해요. 보통 '중무장을 하다', '중무장한 ~'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in stories about the military or police, but people also jokingly call a heavily bundled-up look '중무장' on cold days. It is usually used as '중무장을 하다' or '중무장한 ~'.

examples.en: A break from old ways is needed.

examples.ko: 뱀은 자라면서 탈피를 여러 번 해요.
examples.en: Snakes molt several times as they grow.
I photographed an insect's molting process.
If you want change, start by breaking away from the mold.

examples.ko: 과거 이미지의 탈피를 위해 로고를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: We changed the logo to break away from the old image.
Right after molting, a crab's shell is soft.

explain: 곤충, 뱀, 게가 껍질을 벗을 때도 쓰고, 낡은 생각이나 방식에서 벗어난다는 비유로도 써요. 비유에서는 '낡은 관행에서의 탈피'처럼 조사 '에서'와 함께 써요. 동사는 '탈피하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when insects, snakes or crabs shed their skin, and also figuratively for breaking away from old ideas or ways. In the figurative use it goes with '에서', as in '낡은 관행에서의 탈피'. The verb is '탈피하다'.

examples.en: Residents evacuated because of the flood.
When the evacuation announcement plays, leave right away.
The evacuation site is the school playground.

examples.ko: 할머니는 전쟁 때 피난 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother told me stories about fleeing during the war.
We do evacuation drills every year.
The evacuation was late, and many people suffered.

explain: 재난이나 전쟁 때 위험한 곳을 떠나 안전한 곳으로 가는 것이에요. '대피'는 지금 당장 몸을 피하는 느낌이고, '피난'은 집을 떠나 오래 머무는 경우까지 넓게 써요. '피난을 가다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means leaving a dangerous place for safety during a disaster or war. 대피 feels like getting out of harm's way right now, while 피난 extends to leaving home for a longer stay. The common pattern is 피난을 가다.
